questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good academic opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of assistance from the UNC ISSS. They host a lot of events and you can always schedule a meeting if you need help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Become a member of all the UNC / Chapel Hill off campus housing facebook groups and make a post, people will flood your messages with good offers on off campus housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is way better than living on campus. By all means DO NOT live on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Look at the deadlines for course enrolment, and if you need to join a course where you need prerequisites, write an email to the professor a month or two (at least) before enrolment opens, so that you can register for the course in time. Communication with professors is key, and you're gonna spend a lot of time doing this, but it is necessary of you want the good courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again, the ISSS office will help you, schedule a meeting once in a while if you have any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mostly succesful, I got my mandatory classes because I reached out to the professors a few months ahead of time, and I secured a spot before the classes got full. If I had not done this, my entire exchange program could not have been possible. The courses fill up QUICK, and exchange students are last in line for registration so reach out to professors and make a private agreement before it opens.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Spend a day or two looking at the courses available for your exchange semester and write down which ones you want to take. When the registration opens be quick to secure a spot. And if its a mandatory course for your degree, write an email to the professor.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Took courses from 100-400s (BSc level), I took an extra course such that my workload was 37.5 ECTS instead of 30. Courses are easier, but as you get to 300s and 400s it will get harder, I took two 400s and one 300s and two 100s. It is very hard to fail a class, but also hard to get a good grade. I spent 20-25 hours a week on homework, but its a part of the experience and if you keep up midterms and finals wont be that hard.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more engaging.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the basketball games.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a beach house in Surf City on the coast of NC.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be yourself and talk to people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The tipping culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Americans love dressing up all the time and decorating if there is a football game or halloween etc. There is always something to celebrate so go out and enjoy the festives.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Do not live on campus.
2) Reach out to professors before enrolment opens to secure your spot in a course.
3) Give it 110% socially!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Arrive a week before school starts and get to know the area before it all begins!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The great people I met on my exchange.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the paperwork and emails, you will get there in the end but its a lot work.

questions.question: Any other comments?

questions.answer: Yes
